candidates.status: Retained for CPU feasibility; test allocation not frozen.
candidates.problem: L27 treats checking, strategy changes and ambiguous discourse alike. Useful corrections or alternate methods may be suppressed together with redundant checking.
candidates.paper_component: ATLAS A.2 distinguishes reflection from transition.
candidates.our_design: Keep original L27 extraction, fit, layer, controller, penalty, matcher and reset rules. Replace suppression selection only. First construct a fixed partition of current L27 entries into checking, transition, ambiguous. Do not import all ATLAS words or tune lists on frozen test outcomes.
candidates.important: Examples are proposed assignments, not a frozen full partition or a semantic guarantee. 'another' and 'wait' can have normal semantic uses.
cpu_next: Audit original calibration step text by question, not frozen benchmark correctness, for prefix coverage, co-occurrence and ambiguous usage.
Record exact lexical rules, normalized question hashes and per-category coverage before deciding a candidate.
Compare candidate completion token masks to frozen L27; retain tokenizer identity, multi-token completion, thought opening and clean boundary behavior.
If categories mostly co-occur or disambiguation is not reliable, reject before GPU.
candidates.interface: Separate opt-in table asset supplied to AlignmentAdapter(tables=..., large_suppression=True, enabled=True); retain lexicon_automaton compilation. No shared controller changes.
candidates.state: Use existing per-request lex_state/lex_open/lex_hit and start/end/boundary/reuse resets unchanged. Confidence remains native pre-penalty signal; candidate mask remains gated by negative ReBalance coefficient.
candidates.future_comparison: Frozen L27 versus checking-only and transition-only (mutually exclusive masks, union may exclude ambiguous entries). This identifies category policies but does not isolate semantics from intervention frequency; log attempted/effective mask events and probability mass. Do not call reduced intervention count semantic proof.
candidates.data_cost: No new LLM forward for lexical CPU audit; no regeneration of 500 calibration answers. Later generation needs fixed one-seed comparison and predeclared accuracy loss <=2pp.
candidates.risk: Reduced reflection coverage may lose compression; protecting strategy switches may preserve necessary correction, but switching can itself be redundant.
candidates.stop: Reject if token benefit disappears, accuracy loss exceeds predeclared limit, or apparent benefit is only from failed/incomplete output.

candidates.problem: Token confidence measures model certainty, not whether the current reasoning step is useful or correct.
candidates.paper_component: ATLAS 3.3/3.4 distils PRM step scores into a small latent verifier.
candidates.our_design: Replace only controller decision signal in a future separate arm. Initially compare no steering versus the original ReBalance-proposed action, retain L27 suppression policy; do not simultaneously introduce E/R/T vectors.
candidates.data_cost: Needs question-disjoint training/validation, offline step-quality labels and aligned hidden-state replay. Existing first-content-token features do not automatically equal ATLAS end-of-thought states. PRM labelling and replay require GPU; small-head training cost excludes these.
candidates.cpu_gate: Audit whether labels/states exist and define exact boundary and causal feature availability. No whole-answer correctness copied onto every step.
candidates.risk: Verifier may be miscalibrated on intervened states; argmax over h+v can exploit score without helping downstream reasoning. Natural-state held-out prediction alone cannot validate action ranking.
candidates.interface: Would require explicit opt-in hidden-state read plus batched head at completed step boundary; specify shared interface before implementation. No modification now.
